newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares fall, market nervy over Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares fall, market nervy over Iraq.

text.p: Austrian shares closed lower in line with international markets on Tuesday as concern over the U.S. missile attack on Iraq weighed on sentiment with further losses seen over the next few days.

"Uncertainty has increased after the attack on Iraq," said one trader. "We were resistent to the news at first, but at the end of the day we weren't able to buck the international trend," said another.
The 21-stock ATX blue chip tumbled 11.01 points or 1.07 percent to 1,022.37 points. Among its constituents, 15 losers outnumbered four gainers and two issues closed unchanged.
Traders said the ATX was holding within its current 1,020-1,040 trading range, but predicted it was edging towards the support level.
One said the market lacked strong technical support.
"If we fall below 1,020, it means we could well slide to the 1,000 level," he said.
Another said short-term direction depended on Wall Street and oil prices, which have been rocketing following recent Iraq-U.S. developments.
"Investors are afraid crude prices could soar and that the Dow could take a battering," he said.

Creditanstalt led gainers, jumping 4.2 schillings to 479. One trader said the stock was on a technical rebound after recent losses. Another said gains were a reaction to Finance Minister Viktor Klima's newest remarks on the bank's sale.
Klima on Monday extended the deadline for an Austro-Italian consortium's bid for Creditanstalt, the country's longest-running sell-off candidate, by one week.
"Apparently the holding model is not what investors are looking for," a dealer said.
The session's leading decliner was VA Stahl, which fell 3.2 percent or 11 schillings to 332.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for September delivery were down 11.5 points at 1,019.2.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index shed 2.07 points or 0.5 percent to close at 40.65. -- Vienna newsroom +431 531 12 257
